passages.text: I hope you will bear with a little of my foolishness, but you are already doing that.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the Corinthian church.
\r\nPaul asks the Corinthians to bear with him.
\r\nHe says he may speak with a little foolishness.
\r\nHe hopes they will be patient with him.
\r\nHe notes that they are already being patient with him.
passages.original: Ὄφελον ἀνείχεσθέ μου μικρόν τι ἀφροσύνης ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀνέχεσθέ μου

passages.text: I am jealous for you with a godly jealousy. For I promised you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the Corinthian church.
Paul feels a strong, godly jealousy for the believers.
Paul promised the believers to one husband.
That husband is Christ.
Paul wants to present the believers to Christ.
Paul wants the believers to be pure.
Paul wants the believers to be like a virgin.
Paul wants the believers to belong only to Christ.
passages.original: ζηλῶ γὰρ ὑμᾶς Θεοῦ ζήλῳ ἡρμοσάμην γὰρ ὑμᾶς ἑνὶ ἀνδρὶ παρθένον ἁγνὴν παραστῆσαι τῷ Χριστῷ

passages.text: I am afraid, however, that just as Eve was deceived by the serpent’s cunning, your minds may be led astray from your simple and pure devotion to Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Corinthian church.
Paul is concerned for the believers.
Paul fears something may happen to them.
The serpent deceived Eve by using cunning.
Paul fears their minds may be led astray in a similar way.
He fears they may turn away from simple devotion to Christ.
He fears they may lose their pure devotion to Christ.
passages.original: Φοβοῦμαι δὲ μή πως ὡς ὁ ὄφις ἐξηπάτησεν Εὕαν ἐν τῇ πανουργίᾳ αὐτοῦ φθαρῇ τὰ νοήματα ὑμῶν ἀπὸ τῆς ἁπλότητος καὶ τῆς ἁγνότητος τῆς εἰς τὸν Χριστόν

passages.text: For if someone comes and proclaims a Jesus other than the One we proclaimed, or if you receive a different spirit than the One you received, or a different gospel than the one you accepted, you put up with it way too easily.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Corinthian church.
Paul and his companions proclaimed the true Jesus to the Corinthians.
If someone comes to you and proclaims a different Jesus, that person is not proclaiming the true Jesus.
You did not hear about this other Jesus from us.
If you receive a different spirit, that spirit is not the one you received from us.
If you accept a different gospel, that gospel is not the one you first accepted.
You tolerate these things too easily.
passages.original: εἰ μὲν γὰρ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἄλλον Ἰησοῦν κηρύσσει ὃν οὐκ ἐκηρύξαμεν ἢ πνεῦμα ἕτερον λαμβάνετε ὃ οὐκ ἐλάβετε ἢ εὐαγγέλιον ἕτερον ὃ οὐκ ἐδέξασθε καλῶς ἀνέχεσθε

passages.text: I consider myself in no way inferior to those “super-apostles.”
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul compares himself to the so-called "super-apostles."
Paul says, "I am not less than these 'super-apostles.'"
Paul considers himself equal to them in every way.
Paul does not see himself as inferior to any of them.
passages.original: Λογίζομαι γὰρ μηδὲν ὑστερηκέναι τῶν Ὑπερλίαν ἀποστόλων

passages.text: Although I am not a polished speaker, I am certainly not lacking in knowledge. We have made this clear to you in every way possible.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul is an apostle.
Paul says he is not a polished speaker.
Paul says he does not lack knowledge.
Paul and his companions have shown this to the Corinthians.
They have made this clear in every way.
They have made this clear in everything.
They have made this clear to the Corinthians.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ καὶ ἰδιώτης τῷ λόγῳ ἀλλ’ οὐ τῇ γνώσει ἀλλ’ ἐν παντὶ φανερώσαντες ἐν πᾶσιν εἰς ὑμᾶς

passages.text: Was it a sin for me to humble myself in order to exalt you, because I preached the gospel of God to you free of charge?
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul humbled himself before the Corinthians.
Paul did this so that the Corinthians could be lifted up.
Paul preached the gospel of God to the Corinthians.
Paul did not ask the Corinthians for payment.
Paul gave them the gospel free of charge.
Paul asks if it was a sin for him to humble himself for their sake.
passages.original: Ἢ ἁμαρτίαν ἐποίησα ἐμαυτὸν ταπεινῶν ἵνα ὑμεῖς ὑψωθῆτε ὅτι δωρεὰν τὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ εὐαγγέλιον εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν

passages.text: I robbed other churches by accepting their support in order to serve you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
\r\nPaul served the Corinthian church.
\r\nPaul accepted support from other churches.
\r\nPaul did this to serve the Corinthians.
\r\nPaul did not take support from the Corinthians.
\r\nPaul says, "I took wages from other churches."
\r\nPaul did this for your ministry.
passages.original: ἄλλας ἐκκλησίας ἐσύλησα λαβὼν ὀψώνιον πρὸς τὴν ὑμῶν διακονίαν

passages.text: And when I was with you and in need, I was not a burden to anyone; for the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied my needs. I have refrained from being a burden to you in any way, and I will continue to do so.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul was with the Corinthian believers.
Paul was in need while he was with them.
Paul did not burden anyone among them.
Brothers came from Macedonia.
These brothers supplied what Paul lacked.
Paul kept himself from being a burden to the Corinthians in every way.
Paul will continue to keep himself from being a burden to them.
passages.original: καὶ παρὼν πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ὑστερηθεὶς οὐ κατενάρκησα οὐθενός τὸ γὰρ ὑστέρημά μου προσανεπλήρωσαν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ ἐλθόντες ἀπὸ Μακεδονίας καὶ ἐν παντὶ ἀβαρῆ ἐμαυτὸν ὑμῖν ἐτήρησα καὶ τηρήσω

passages.text: As surely as the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting of mine will not be silenced in the regions of Achaia.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul speaks the truth of Christ.
The truth of Christ lives in Paul.
Paul boasts about his ministry.
No one will silence Paul's boasting.
Paul will continue to boast in the regions of Achaia.
passages.original: ἔστιν ἀλήθεια Χριστοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ ὅτι ἡ καύχησις αὕτη οὐ φραγήσεται εἰς ἐμὲ ἐν τοῖς κλίμασιν τῆς Ἀχαΐας

passages.text: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the Corinthians.
Paul asks a question.
He says, "Why do I do this?"
He asks, "Is it because I do not love you?"
Paul answers his own question.
He says, "God knows that I do love you."
passages.original: διὰ τί ὅτι οὐκ ἀγαπῶ ὑμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς οἶδεν

passages.text: But I will keep on doing what I am doing, in order to undercut those who want an opportunity to be regarded as our equals in the things of which they boast.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
\r\nPaul acts with the truth of Christ in him.
\r\nPaul continues his current actions.
\r\nPaul will keep doing these things.
\r\nPaul does this to remove the opportunity from certain people.
\r\nThese people want a chance to boast.
\r\nThey want to appear equal to Paul and his companions.
\r\nPaul acts so that these people will not be found equal to him and his companions in what they boast about.
passages.original: Ὃ δὲ ποιῶ καὶ ποιήσω ἵνα ἐκκόψω τὴν ἀφορμὴν τῶν θελόντων ἀφορμήν ἵνα ἐν ᾧ καυχῶνται εὑρεθῶσιν καθὼς καὶ ἡμεῖς

passages.text: For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, masquerading as apostles of Christ.
passages.sermon:
Some men claim to be apostles of Christ.
These men are not true apostles.
They are false apostles.
They work with deceit.
They pretend to be apostles of Christ.
They are actually deceitful workers.
passages.original: οἱ γὰρ τοιοῦτοι ψευδαπόστολοι ἐργάται δόλιοι μετασχηματιζόμενοι εἰς ἀποστόλους Χριστοῦ

passages.text: And no wonder, for Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light.
passages.sermon:
Satan is the enemy of God.
Satan pretends to be good.
Satan disguises himself as an angel.
Satan appears to be full of light.
This is not surprising.
passages.original: καὶ οὐ θαῦμα αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ Σατανᾶς μετασχηματίζεται εἰς ἄγγελον φωτός

passages.text: It is not surprising, then, if his servants masquerade as servants of righteousness. Their end will correspond to their actions.
passages.sermon:
Satan has servants.
These servants pretend to be servants of righteousness.
This is not surprising.
God will judge them by their actions.
Their end will match what they have done.
passages.original: οὐ μέγα οὖν εἰ καὶ οἱ διάκονοι αὐτοῦ μετασχηματίζονται ὡς διάκονοι δικαιοσύνης ὧν τὸ τέλος ἔσται κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν

passages.text: I repeat: Let no one take me for a fool. But if you do, then receive me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the Corinthians.
Paul repeats his message.
Paul says, "Do not think I am a fool."
If you do think I am a fool, then accept me as a fool.
If you accept me as a fool, I can boast a little.
passages.original: Πάλιν λέγω μή τίς με δόξῃ ἄφρονα εἶναι εἰ δὲ μή¦γε κἂν ὡς ἄφρονα δέξασθέ με ἵνα κἀγὼ μικρόν τι καυχήσωμαι

passages.text: In this confident boasting of mine, I am not speaking as the Lord would, but as a fool.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking.
Paul is not speaking as the Lord would speak.
Paul is speaking as a fool.
Paul is boasting with confidence.
Paul admits this way of speaking is foolish.
passages.original: ὃ λαλῶ οὐ κατὰ Κύριον λαλῶ ἀλλ’ ὡς ἐν ἀφροσύνῃ ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ ὑποστάσει τῆς καυχήσεως

passages.text: Since many are boasting according to the flesh, I too will boast.
passages.sermon: Many people boast about things of the flesh.\r\nI will also boast.
passages.original: ἐπεὶ πολλοὶ καυχῶνται κατὰ τὴν σάρκα κἀγὼ καυχήσομαι

passages.text: For you gladly tolerate fools, since you are so wise.
passages.sermon: You are wise.\r\nYou gladly tolerate fools.
passages.original: ἡδέως γὰρ ἀνέχεσθε τῶν ἀφρόνων φρόνιμοι ὄντες

passages.text: In fact, you even put up with anyone who enslaves you or exploits you or takes advantage of you or exalts himself or strikes you in the face.
passages.sermon:
You tolerate people who treat you badly.
You put up with anyone who makes you a slave.
You accept it when someone takes what belongs to you.
You allow people to take advantage of you.
You let people act proudly over you.
You even endure it when someone hits you in the face.
passages.original: ἀνέχεσθε γὰρ εἴ τις ὑμᾶς καταδουλοῖ εἴ τις κατεσθίει εἴ τις λαμβάνει εἴ τις ἐπαίρεται εἴ τις εἰς πρόσωπον ὑμᾶς δέρει

passages.text: To my shame I concede that we were too weak for that! Speaking as a fool, however, I can match what anyone else dares to boast about.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul feels shame.
Paul admits that he and his companions were too weak for such things.
Paul now speaks as if he were a fool.
Paul says he can dare to boast just as much as anyone else.
passages.original: κατὰ ἀτιμίαν λέγω ὡς ὅτι ἡμεῖς ἠσθενήκαμεν Ἐν ᾧ δ’ ἄν τις τολμᾷ ἐν ἀφροσύνῃ λέγω τολμῶ κἀγώ

passages.text: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking about himself and his opponents.
Paul asks, "Are they Hebrews?"
Paul says, "I am a Hebrew too."
Paul asks, "Are they Israelites?"
Paul says, "I am an Israelite too."
Paul asks, "Are they descendants of Abraham?"
Paul says, "I am a descendant of Abraham too."
passages.original: Ἑβραῖοί εἰσιν κἀγώ Ἰσραηλῖταί εἰσιν κἀγώ σπέρμα Ἀβραάμ εἰσιν κἀγώ

passages.text: Are they servants of Christ? I am speaking like I am out of my mind, but I am so much more: in harder labor, in more imprisonments, in worse beatings, in frequent danger of death.
passages.sermon:
They claim to be servants of Christ.
I am also a servant of Christ.
I speak boldly now.
I have worked much harder than they have.
I have been imprisoned more often than they have.
I have been beaten more severely than they have.
I have faced death many times.
passages.original: διάκονοι Χριστοῦ εἰσιν παραφρονῶν λαλῶ ὑπὲρ ἐγώ ἐν κόποις περισσοτέρως ἐν φυλακαῖς περισσοτέρως ἐν πληγαῖς ὑπερβαλλόντως ἐν θανάτοις πολλάκις

passages.text: Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul is a servant of Christ.
Paul is an Israelite.
Paul is a descendant of Abraham.
The Jews punished Paul.
Five times, the Jews gave Paul thirty-nine lashes.
passages.original: Ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων πεντάκις τεσσεράκοντα παρὰ μίαν ἔλαβον

passages.text: Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked. I spent a night and a day in the open sea.
passages.sermon:
Paul is a servant of Christ.
Paul suffered many hardships.
Three times, people beat Paul with rods.
Once, people stoned Paul.
Three times, Paul was shipwrecked.
Paul spent a night and a day in the open sea.
passages.original: τρὶς ἐραβδίσθην ἅπαξ ἐλιθάσθην τρὶς ἐναυάγησα νυχθήμερον ἐν τῷ βυθῷ πεποίηκα

passages.text: In my frequent journeys, I have been in danger from rivers and from bandits, in danger from my countrymen and from the Gentiles, in danger in the city and in the country, in danger on the sea and among false brothers, in labor and toil and often without sleep, in hunger and thirst and often without food, in cold and exposure.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul often traveled on many journeys.
Paul faced danger from rivers.
Paul faced danger from bandits.
Paul faced danger from his own people, the Jews.
Paul faced danger from Gentiles.
Paul faced danger in cities.
Paul faced danger in the countryside.
Paul faced danger at sea.
Paul faced danger from false brothers.
Paul worked hard and labored much.
Paul often went without sleep.
Paul was hungry and thirsty many times.
Paul often had no food.
Paul was cold and lacked proper clothing.
passages.original: ὁδοιπορίαις πολλάκις κινδύνοις ποταμῶν κινδύνοις λῃστῶν κινδύνοις ἐκ γένους κινδύνοις ἐξ ἐθνῶν κινδύνοις ἐν πόλει κινδύνοις ἐν ἐρημίᾳ κινδύνοις ἐν θαλάσσῃ κινδύνοις ἐν ψευδαδέλφοις κόπῳ καὶ μόχθῳ ἐν ἀγρυπνίαις πολλάκις ἐν λιμῷ καὶ δίψει ἐν νηστείαις πολλάκις ἐν ψύχει καὶ γυμνότητι

passages.text: Apart from these external trials, I face daily the pressure of my concern for all the churches.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul suffers many external trials.
These trials include beatings, shipwrecks, dangers, hunger, and cold.
Apart from these external trials, Paul faces another burden.
Every day, Paul feels pressure.
This pressure comes from his concern for all the churches.
passages.original: Χωρὶς τῶν παρεκτὸς ἡ ἐπίστασίς μοι ἡ καθ’ ἡμέραν ἡ μέριμνα πασῶν τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν

passages.text: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is led into sin, and I do not burn with grief?
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
\r\nPaul cares deeply for the churches.
\r\nIf someone is weak, I also feel weak.
\r\nIf someone falls into sin, I am filled with grief.
passages.original: τίς ἀσθενεῖ καὶ οὐκ ἀσθενῶ τίς σκανδαλίζεται καὶ οὐκ ἐγὼ πυροῦμαι

passages.text: If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul sometimes needs to speak about himself.
If Paul must boast, he will not boast about his strengths.
Paul will boast about the things that show his weakness.
passages.original: Εἰ καυχᾶσθαι δεῖ τὰ τῆς ἀσθενείας μου καυχήσομαι

passages.text: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is forever worthy of praise, knows that I am not lying.
passages.sermon: God is the Father of the Lord Jesus.\r\nGod is forever worthy of praise.\r\nGod knows that I am not lying.
passages.original: ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Πατὴρ τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ οἶδεν ὁ ὢν εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας ὅτι οὐ ψεύδομαι

passages.text: In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas secured the city of the Damascenes in order to arrest me.
passages.sermon:
I was in Damascus.
King Aretas ruled at that time.
The governor served under King Aretas.
The governor guarded the city of Damascus.
He wanted to arrest me.
passages.original: ἐν Δαμασκῷ ὁ ἐθνάρχης Ἁρέτα τοῦ βασιλέως ἐφρούρει τὴν πόλιν Δαμασκηνῶν πιάσαι με

passages.text: But I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped his grasp.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul was in danger in Damascus.
Someone wanted to arrest Paul.
Paul escaped.
People lowered Paul in a basket.
They lowered him through a window.
The window was in the city wall.
Paul escaped from the man who wanted to catch him.
passages.original: καὶ διὰ θυρίδος ἐν σαργάνῃ ἐχαλάσθην διὰ τοῦ τείχους καὶ ἐξέφυγον τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ
